clusters.name: NREM Parasomnias (Sleepwalking & Sleep Terrors)
items: Incomplete awakening from N3 slow-wave sleep during first third of night (DSM p.452)
Sleepwalking: blank staring face, unresponsiveness, difficult awakening (DSM p.452)
Sleep Terrors: panicky scream, intense fear, autonomic arousal (mydriasis, tachycardia, sweating) (DSM p.452)
Amnesia for the episode and no/minimal dream recall (DSM p.452)

clusters.name: REM Sleep Behavior Disorder (RBD)
items: Recurrent vocalizations or complex motor behaviors during REM sleep (DSM p.461)
Dream-enactment behaviors reflecting violent/action dreams (DSM p.461)
Immediate full alertness and orientation upon awakening without confusion (DSM p.461)
REM sleep without atonia documented on PSG or established synucleinopathy (DSM p.461)

clusters.name: Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS)
items: Urge to move legs usually accompanied by uncomfortable sensations (DSM p.464)
Urge begins or worsens during periods of rest or inactivity (DSM p.464)
Urge is partially or totally relieved by movement (DSM p.465)
Urge is worse or exclusively occurs in the evening or night (DSM p.465)

subtypes: Sleepwalking specifiers: With sleep-related eating, With sleep-related sexual behavior (Sexsomnia) (DSM p.452)
RLS presentations: Familial early-onset (<45 years) vs. Late-onset (DSM p.466)

epidemiology.prevalence: RLS: 2%-4% in children (Dulcan p.485), 1.6% in adults (DSM p.465); NREM Sleepwalking: 14%-40% isolated, 5% annual in children (DSM p.454, Dulcan p.487); Sleep Terrors: 3%-6% in children (Dulcan p.488); RBD: 1%-2% in older adults (DSM p.462)
epidemiology.sex_ratio: RLS: 2:1 F:M in adults (DSM p.465); RBD: Predominantly M (>50 years) (DSM p.462); NREM Sleepwalking: F>M in children, equal in adults (DSM p.454); Sleep Terrors: M>F in children (DSM p.454)
epidemiology.onset_age_typical: Sleepwalking: 4-12 years peak (Dulcan p.488); Sleep Terrors: 1.5-10 years peak (Dulcan p.488); RLS: 10-30 years typical (DSM p.466); RBD: >50 years (DSM p.462)
epidemiology.heritability: NREM Parasomnias: up to 80% family history, 60% risk if both parents sleepwalk (DSM p.454); RLS: up to 80% familial in young-onset (DSM p.466)
comorbidities: RLS with ADHD: ~25% bidirectional overlap in children (Dulcan p.485, p.491)
RLS with PLMS: up to 90% (DSM p.465)
Idiopathic RBD with Synucleinopathies (Parkinson's, DLB, MSA): 75% conversion (DSM p.462)
epidemiology.prognosis: NREM Parasomnias: transient, 50%-65% remission by adolescence (DSM p.454, Dulcan p.487); RBD: 75% convert to neurodegenerative disease over 10-15 years (DSM p.462); RLS: chronic progressive course (DSM p.466)

etiology.genetic: MEIS1 gene variant doubles RLS risk (DSM p.467); Polygenic inheritance in NREM parasomnias (DSM p.454)
etiology.neurobiology: RLS: central dopamine dysfunction (A11 diencephalospinal group) & central iron deficiency affecting Tyrosine Hydroxylase (DSM p.467, Dulcan p.485, StahlNeuro p.85); RBD: loss of REM atonia via pontine/medullary brainstem degeneration & alpha-synuclein deposition (DSM p.463, StahlNeuro p.506); NREM: incomplete arousal dissociation from N3 slow-wave sleep (DSM p.455)
etiology.environmental: Sleep deprivation, fever, physical/emotional stress trigger NREM parasomnias (DSM p.454, Dulcan p.488); Pregnancy, uremia, SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs, antihistamines, and dopamine antagonists exacerbate RLS (DSM p.467, Dulcan p.485)

first_line: RLS: Oral elemental iron 3-6 mg/kg/day if serum ferritin <50 ng/mL (Dulcan p.485)
Parasomnias: Environmental safety precautions & strict sleep hygiene (Dulcan p.488)
Sleep Terrors: Scheduled awakenings 15-20 min before usual event time (Dulcan p.488)
second_line: RLS: Dopamine agonists (Ropinirole, Pramipexole, Rotigotine) or Alpha-2-Delta ligands (Gabapentin, Pregabalin) (Dulcan p.485-486, StahlNeuro p.397, p.557)
Severe Parasomnias/RBD: Clonazepam 0.01 mg/kg (0.125-1.0 mg hs) (Dulcan p.482, p.488)
Refractory Parasomnias: Clonidine 0.025-0.3 mg hs (Dulcan p.482, StahlKids p.139)
key_side_effects: Dopaminergic Augmentation in RLS (earlier daily onset & worsening symptoms) (StahlNeuro p.530)
Clonazepam sedation, ataxia, and tolerance (Dulcan p.482)
treatment.monitoring: Serum ferritin every 3-4 months in RLS until target 80-100 ng/mL is reached (Dulcan p.485)

items: BEARS pediatric sleep screening tool covering 5 clinical domains (Dulcan p.475)
Polysomnography (PSG) showing REM sleep without atonia required for definitive RBD diagnosis (DSM p.461, p.463)
2-week sleep log/diary for tracking sleep-wake regularity (Dulcan p.475, DSM p.420)
Serum ferritin level check mandatory in pediatric RLS assessment (Dulcan p.485)
key_numbers: 5 domains in BEARS screening tool (Bedtime, Excessive daytime sleepiness, Awakenings, Regularity, Snoring) (Dulcan p.475)
50 ng/mL serum ferritin threshold requiring iron replacement in RLS (Dulcan p.485)
90% of RLS patients demonstrate Periodic Limb Movements in Sleep (PLMS) on PSG (DSM p.465)
14 days (2 weeks) standard duration for sleep log/diary monitoring (Dulcan p.475)

items: Nightmare Disorder: occurs during REM sleep in second half of night, vivid dream recall, full alertness, minimal autonomic arousal (DSM p.455, p.460)
Nocturnal Seizures: stereotyped brief motor movements, multiple per night, EEG epileptiform discharges (DSM p.456, p.464)
Medication-induced Akathisia: global body restlessness caused by dopamine antagonists, lacks evening worsening or relief by walking (DSM p.467, StahlKids p.153)
Growing Pains: deep nocturnal leg pain in children without urge to move or relief by walking (Dulcan p.499)
Nocturnal Leg Cramps: painful muscle contractions resolved by single stretch without urge to move (DSM p.467)
key_numbers: 3 times per week for 3 months threshold distinguishes RLS from transient leg cramps (DSM p.465)
10 to 15 years latency between RBD onset and neurodegenerative synucleinopathy manifestation (DSM p.462)

high_yield: NREM parasomnias occur in N3 slow-wave sleep during the first third of the night, featuring complete amnesia, lack of dream recall, and impaired arousal (DSM p.452).
Idiopathic RBD is a major prodromal marker for alpha-synucleinopathies, with 75% of patients converting to Parkinson's disease, DLB, or MSA within 10-15 years (DSM p.462).
RBD in children or young adults is extremely rare and necessitates immediate evaluation for Narcolepsy, SSRI use, or brainstem lesions (DSM p.462).
RLS diagnosis requires all 4 core criteria: urge to move legs, worse at rest, relieved by movement, and worse in the evening/night (DSM p.464-465).
First-line medical treatment for pediatric RLS is oral elemental iron (3-6 mg/kg/day) when serum ferritin is <50 ng/mL, targeting 80-100 ng/mL (Dulcan p.485).
RLS has a bidirectional ~25% comorbidity with ADHD in pediatric populations (Dulcan p.485, p.491).
SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs, first-generation antihistamines, and dopamine receptor antagonists exacerbate RLS and PLMS (DSM p.467, Dulcan p.485).
